headline: Russia to dispatch FIRST diesel cargo to US on Thursday (40,000 tons)
dek: Novak: vessel carrying 40,000 metric tons departs Thursday; 'additional shipments will follow... We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities.' Trump promised 300,000 tons 'immediately' (2.25m barrels), then 500,000 in Nov, 1m 'immediately thereafter'.
sources: Deputy PM Alexander Novak via Vedomosti/RIA (shipment); Reuters analysis 'Global diesel prices seen staying high despite Trump's deal' (Oct 21)
fault_line: Gift to Putin or genuine price relief — and who actually gets the diesel, America or the world?

sections.what_happened: Novak: vessel carrying 40,000 metric tons departs Thursday; 'additional shipments will follow... We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities.' Trump promised 300,000 tons 'immediately' (2.25m barrels), then 500,000 in Nov, 1m 'immediately thereafter'. BUT Kpler: need +400,000 bpd to move market; first shipment = ~73,000 bpd over a month — 'would probably not significantly affect global diesel prices.' Baringa: need 850,000 bpd for immediate softening. Trump later said cargoes go to GLOBAL markets, not US (Rubio confirmed). During Witkoff-Putin talks, Witkoff thanked Putin for lifting export restrictions.
sections.what_verified: Reuters; RIA/Vedomosti; Novak named source; Kpler/Baringa estimates; Witkoff-Putin readout corroborates deal live
sections.what_disputed: 40,000 tons is far below Trump's promised 300,000 tons 'immediate'; no named port; first cargo to GLOBAL markets per Trump/Rubio — domestic price relief unclear; Russia's export ban lift conditional on domestic shortages (Ukrainian refinery strikes)
sections.why_matters: The headline numbers don't survive the math: the 'immediate' 40,000 tons is a drop in the market Kpler says needs 400,000 barrels a day
sections.context: Background: Energy — NEW on diesel-deal thread: Russia to dispatch FIRST diesel cargo to US on Thursday (40,000 tons); Reuters analysis: prices will stay high anyway

totw_analysis: Our read: The headline numbers don't survive the math: the 'immediate' 40,000 tons is a drop in the market Kpler says needs 400,000 barrels a day The fault line our audience is arguing over: Gift to Putin or genuine price relief — and who actually gets the diesel, America or the world?
